CallDetail.description:
`GET /calls/{call_id}`: everything the call review screen renders.

Analysis fields are None/empty until the analysis task has finished. An
uploaded recording is `transcribing` until the ASR worker is done, with an
empty transcript and no turns; the upload screen polls this.
CallDetail.title: CallDetail

CallStatus.description:
Where a call sits in the *service* lifecycle — the `calls.status` column.

Deliberately separate from `sawti.agent.state.ReviewStatus`, which is graph
bookkeeping inside one run. This one also covers what happens around the
graph (waiting in the queue, infrastructure failure). The mapping:

    transcribing    — uploaded audio waiting for, or in, the native ASR
                      worker (phase 6.4); no transcript yet.
    queued          — no graph run yet; no checkpoint thread exists.
    processing      — the graph is running (ReviewStatus "pending").
    awaiting_review — the graph is suspended in `escalate`
                      (ReviewStatus "awaiting_human").
    reviewed        — a reviewer resumed it (ReviewStatus "human_reviewed").
    completed       — auto-passed, no human needed (ReviewStatus "auto_passed").
    failed          — the task gave up after retries. No graph equivalent:
                      a graph-level `error` routes to `escalate`, i.e. to
                      `awaiting_review`, never here.
CallStatus.title: CallStatus

ClaimChanges.description:
The structured fields a `correct` verdict changes — only the ones the reviewer set.

"Set" is literal: a field absent from the request is unchanged. For
`deadline`, an explicit `null` removes the deadline; every other field
must be given a value if present. Which fields apply depends on the
claim's kind (`EDITABLE_FIELDS`); the route rejects the rest. The
evidence quote is not editable: it is what the transcript says.
ClaimChanges.title: ClaimChanges

ConflictResolveRequest.description:
`POST /memory/conflicts/{id}/resolve`.

* `keep_existing`: the candidate is dropped; existing rules untouched.
* `keep_new`: the conflicting rules are retired; the candidate becomes active.
* `discard`: neither. The candidate is dropped and the conflicting rules retired.
* `not_a_conflict`: the detector was wrong. The candidate becomes active,
  existing rules untouched; counted in `/stats` as a false positive.
ConflictResolveRequest.title: ConflictResolveRequest

ReviewSubmission.description:
`POST /reviews/{call_id}/corrections`: one verdict per grounded claim.

The route rejects the submission (422) unless the claim ids are exactly the
call's grounded claims — none missing, none unknown — and every `correct`
actually changes its claim. Mapping onto `sawti.schemas.Correction`: each
`reject` / `correct` verdict becomes one `Correction` whose `corrected`
differs from `original` in structured fields (`reject`: the claim is
removed; `correct`: the changes are applied), at an `error_location`
`sawti.memory.induction` can render (`sawti.api.records.plan_corrections`).
`confirm` verdicts produce no `Correction`; the whole submission is stored
as a `ReviewSubmission` row. See docs/09-DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-07.
ReviewSubmission.title: ReviewSubmission

post.description:
Redact the transcript, store the redacted text only, and queue the call for analysis.

The raw transcript exists only inside this function; it is neither stored
nor put into graph state (docs/09-DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-06, decision 1).

Returns 422 if a line has no `Agent:`/`Customer:` prefix (the review
screen needs speaker turns, and the parser does not guess), and 503 if
the task could not be queued — the call is then marked `failed`.

Store an uploaded recording and queue it for the native ASR worker.

The call is `transcribing` until the worker has transcribed, diarized and
redacted it (the same redaction as `POST /calls`); it is then `queued` for
analysis like any submitted transcript. Poll `GET /calls/{id}`.

Raw audio is PII: it stays only in `SAWTI_AUDIO_DIR` until transcription
ends, and is then deleted unless `SAWTI_KEEP_AUDIO=true`.

Returns 413 over the size limit, 415 for anything but wav/mp3/m4a (by
extension *and* content), 422 for an empty file or missing form fields,
and 503 if the ASR task could not be queued (the call is then `failed`).

The size limit is enforced while copying into `SAWTI_AUDIO_DIR`, after
Starlette has spooled the multipart body to a temporary file. A huge
upload is therefore received before it is refused. That is acceptable for
a localhost-only service (docs/09-DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-10); a deployed
one would cap the body size in front of the app.

get.description: Everything the call review screen renders. Analysis fields are empty until analysis finishes.
200 when both dependencies answer, 503 (with which one failed) otherwise.
Unresolved conflicts, oldest first: each candidate beside the rules it contradicts.

post.description:
Apply a reviewer's decision. 404 unknown, 409 already resolved, 503 while the store is being written.

An action that activates the candidate queues consolidation on the worker
(the API has no embedding model). The resolution itself is already
committed if that enqueue fails; `consolidation_queued` then says so, and
the next induction run consolidates the whole store anyway.

get.description: Active (non-retired) rules, newest first, with their source languages and usage.
The cloud vs self-hosted table and the memory comparison. 503 if a results file is missing.
Calls in `status` (default `awaiting_review`), oldest first, plus per-language pending counts.

post.description:
Record a reviewer's verdicts, capture the corrections, and queue the graph's resume.

409 if the call is not `awaiting_review` or already has a submission;
422 unless there is exactly one verdict for every grounded claim. The
submission, its `Correction`s and the `ReviewerAction` rows commit as one
unit before the resume is queued. If the review produced corrections, rule
induction over them is queued too (`induce_rules_task`).

get.description: Pending reviews, reviewer agreement, active rules and conflict false positives, per language.
